title: Does Earth’s Magnetic Field Affect Aging? - Nautilus
gist: A study in the journal Aging from Lisa Chakrabarti's group at Nottingham removes Earth's magnetic field in experiments to test whether it affects cellular aging, possibly through the mitochondria. The excerpt is a teaser with no results.

insights.claim: Researchers at Nottingham, publishing in Aging, are testing whether Earth's magnetic field affects aging by removing the field in experiments.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: An early lead in longevity science, where any environmental factor in cell aging could open new research directions.
insights.quote: A new study published in the journal Aging is aiming to correct this by making that field disappear

insights.claim: The article frames the mitochondria as the possible link between Earth's magnetic field and aging.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Mitochondrial function is a core target for the longevity and biotech industry.
insights.locator: The secret may lie in the mitochondria

insights.claim: Scientists still know surprisingly little about whether and how Earth's magnetic field affects how cells work, even though every organism lives inside it.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Points to a little-studied variable in biology, which also bears on long-duration spaceflight where the geomagnetic field is weak.
insights.quote: yet we know surprisingly little about whether and how this invisible force affects the way our cells work
